newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel steady, more Russian straight-run seen July.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel steady, more Russian straight-run seen July.

text.p: European fuel oil markets traded quietly on Friday with prices steady to slightly weaker and Russian straight-run still sought after, traders said.

High sulphur barges were heard traded at $80.25 a tonne early in the day before business settled into a pattern with offers around the $81.50-$82 level and bids at $80 and $80.50. Yesterday's high and low of $83 and $79 were not heard repeated.
Low sulphur prices faded $1 a tonne to $93/$95 under a little pressure from poorer swaps, traders said.
Low sulphur straight-run prices firmed overnight on crude's gains, with one seller heard to be refusing bids of $106 fob a tonne for average quality material.
Sellers were in no hurry to trade, with perceived short supply until mid-June boosting their position.
Scarce Russian straight-run maintained its healthy premia but prospects looked good for healthier supply into June.

"The Russian has been attractive because of the good margins but it must cool down now because the economics are turning around and sellers say there is a little bit more straight-run due from mid-June," one trader said.
With a fourth mother-ship docked at St.Petersburg this week to tranship barge material and a fifth storage vessel due on station next week more straight-run should appear, he added.

The Norsi refinery at Nizhni Novgorod, east of Moscow, would also pump out more straight-run for export, one trader said, as a result of oil giant Lukoil taking over management of the complex and boosting crude runs.
"We've seen two good M100s in close succession out of Klaipeda from Noris and we're told there is more to follow," said the trader.
